title: Mailing Presumption Receipt
subject: Evidence
stem: A charter confirmation sent by mail is the center of dispute in this case. Rebekah, who operates a charter fishing service, sues Phoebe in federal court for the full charter fee after Phoebe failed to confirm the booking before the stated deadline. At trial, Rebekah proves she sent the charter confirmation by mail to Phoebe's home address nineteen days before the booking date. Phoebe testifies she never received it. Rebekah asks the judge to instruct the jury on the legal effect of that mailing. Which instruction is proper?

choices.A: The jury may infer that Phoebe received the confirmation from proof of the mailing, but must determine receipt after weighing Phoebe's denial.
choices.B: The jury may consider the mailing evidence only to assess Phoebe's credibility, not as proof that she received the confirmation.
choices.C: The jury must find that Phoebe received the confirmation because Rebekah proved the mailing.
choices.D: The jury may consider the confirmation only if Rebekah also introduces records of every other piece of mail she sent to Phoebe that season.

rightExplanation: Under FRE 301, the mailing presumption is rebuttable. Once Phoebe produces contrary evidence — her own denial of receipt — the presumption bursts under the Thayer bursting-bubble model adopted by FRE 301. The presumption dissolves, but the underlying inference survives: proof of proper mailing is still probative evidence that the confirmation was received. The jury may infer receipt from the mailing proof, but it must weigh that inference against Phoebe's denial. A directed verdict on receipt would be proper only if Phoebe produced no rebuttal evidence; she did. The jury decides.

wrongExplanations.B: Mailing evidence is substantive — it tends to prove that the confirmation was received. Restricting it to credibility assessment strips it of its probative value on the central fact. No rule limits this evidence to impeachment use only.
wrongExplanations.C: This states a conclusive presumption: once mailing is proven, receipt is compelled. FRE 301 creates only rebuttable presumptions in civil cases. Directing the jury to find receipt after contrary evidence is introduced would bypass the jury's factfinding role. The presumption is not conclusive.
wrongExplanations.D: The rule of completeness (FRE 106) requires completing a partial written or recorded statement when fairness demands — not producing every document of the same kind. Rebekah must produce the confirmation itself; she need not introduce every other piece of mail she sent that season.
